title: Unemployment insurance wage report and contributions
summary: Maryland employers must register for an unemployment insurance account and, every quarter, report gross wages and pay unemployment insurance tax within one month of the quarter's end. Late reports cost $35 each, and late payments add interest of 1.5% a month.
action: Register and file in BEACON, the state's unemployment insurance portal. Pay by e-check when you file.

recurring.label: Unemployment insurance wage report and contributions, {period}

sourceName: Maryland Department of Labor: Tax rates and quarterly reporting

title: Employer withholding return (MW506)
summary: Employers must withhold Maryland income tax from wages and send it to the Comptroller. Employers who withhold more than $700 in any quarter file monthly, due the 15th of the next month. Smaller employers file quarterly, due the 15th of the month after the quarter.
action: Register for a withholding account with the Comptroller, then file and pay on the schedule the Comptroller assigns you. Dates shown assume monthly filing.
frequencyNote: Monthly if you withhold over $700 in a quarter, otherwise quarterly
sourceName: Comptroller of Maryland: Employer Withholding Guide

title: Annual withholding reconciliation (MW508) and W-2s to employees
summary: By January 31 each year, give every employee a W-2 and file the MW508 annual reconciliation of last year's Maryland withholding. Employers with 25 or more W-2s must file electronically.
action: File MW508 with the Comptroller and hand out W-2s by January 31.

recurring.label: MW508 reconciliation and W-2s for {period} wages

sourceName: Comptroller of Maryland: Employer Withholding Guide

title: Carry workers' compensation insurance
summary: With few exceptions, every Maryland employer with one or more employees must have workers' compensation coverage from an insurer licensed in Maryland. The Commission assesses penalties on employers without it.
action: Buy a policy from a licensed insurer (Chesapeake Employers' Insurance Company is the state's guaranteed-market insurer) and keep it active.
sourceName: Maryland Workers' Compensation Commission: Employer FAQs

title: Offer a retirement plan or enroll in MarylandSaves
summary: Established Maryland businesses that use an automated payroll system must either offer a retirement plan or sign employees up for MarylandSaves, the state's program. Businesses that do get their $300 SDAT annual report fee waived each year. There are no employer fees or contributions.
action: If you don't offer a retirement plan, enroll at MarylandSaves. If you already offer one, you can still claim the SDAT fee waiver through MarylandSaves.
